chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUbayd Allāh al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

There is no harm in iqʿāʾ during salat (prayer) between the two sajdahs. The proper understanding of this narration is concession or a state of necessity, except that what we have previously presented in the first narration is more virtuous; and that also accords with the narrations that we cited in our major book, and this also confirms that.

key_terms.الرُّخْصَةُ: A legal concession indicating permissibility in a less preferred mode.
key_terms.الرِّوَايَةِ الْأُولَى: The earlier narration referred to as establishing the preferred practice.
key_terms.السَّجْدَتَيْنِ: The two prostrations between which this sitting posture occurs.
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: The ritual prayer in which the posture is being discussed.
key_terms.الضَّرُورَةِ: A state of necessity that justifies acting upon the concession.
key_terms.الْأَفْضَلَ: That which is more virtuous or preferable in practice.
key_terms.الْإِقْعَاءِ: A particular sitting posture in salat (prayer), especially between the two sajdahs.

ai.seo_question: Is iqʿāʾ between the two sajdahs in salat (prayer) permissible in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This text states that iqʿāʾ between the two sajdahs in salat (prayer) is not prohibited. However, it explains that this permissibility is understood as a concession or for a state of necessity, while the more excellent practice is the one mentioned in the earlier narration.
